What does the AI voice receptionist do for a shop? It answers the shop phone when you can't — mid-cut, on a job, after hours — talks to the caller like a front desk would, books the appointment or takes a callback request, and sends the owner a short summary. It isn't on real shop phones yet; the demo at albanyaiguy.com/shop-line shows how it works. What is the Albany trunk line? One local number for the Capital Region. You call, say what you need (a haircut, a heating repair, a plumber), and the line finds a qualifying local shop and sends it your request. The shop confirms the time or calls you back. Bookings only go to shops that have opted in. Which areas does it cover? Albany, Schenectady, Rensselaer, and Saratoga counties first, then the wider 518 by request. How do I join the pilot? Email hello@albanyaiguy.com with your shop's name, what kind of business it is, and your town. I'll reply personally. Is it for emergencies? No. For medical, fire, or police emergencies call 911. If you smell gas, leave first, then call 911 or your gas utility's emergency line. Join the pilot Run a 518 shop? Pilot it with me. I'm starting with a small group of Albany-area shops. /tips: Albany, NY · 518 · Free tips AI tips you can use today Simple rule I build by: easier is cool. These are the prompts I tell people about first. Copy one into any free AI assistant (ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini, Claude), fill in the brackets, and go. No sign-up here, and this page doesn't save anything you do. For anyone Prep any phone call in 30 seconds Doctor’s office, insurance, the cable company, a landlord. You go in with a plan and hang up with the answer instead of a callback. The prompt Be my call-prep helper. Ask me who I’m calling and what the problem is. Then give me a 30-second script of exactly what to say, and the 3 questions I should ask so I don’t have to call back. Keep it short and plain. Copy prompt : Prep any phone call in 30 seconds Open in ChatGPT with the prompt for Prep any phone call in 30 seconds (opens in a new tab) For shop owners Write the text that goes out when you miss a call Most people who hit voicemail call the next shop. A quick text back keeps them. Your phone carrier or booking app can usually send it automatically. The prompt I own a [type of business] in Albany, NY. Write 3 versions of a short text message (under 160 characters) that goes out automatically when I miss a call. It should say who we are, that we saw the call, and give one easy next step (reply with what you need, or a booking link). Friendly, no emojis, no pressure. Copy prompt : Write the text that goes out when you miss a call Open in ChatGPT with the prompt for Write the text that goes out when you miss a call (opens in a new tab) For shop owners Fix your voicemail greeting A greeting that tells people what to leave (name, number, what they need, best time) gets you messages you can actually act on. The prompt Write a 20-second voicemail greeting for my [type of business] in [town]. Include our hours, ask the caller to leave their name, number, what they need and the best time to call back, and mention one faster option (text this number, or book at [website]). Sound like a real person, not a robot. Copy prompt : Fix your voicemail greeting Open in ChatGPT with the prompt for Fix your voicemail greeting (opens in a new tab) For shop owners Turn your reviews into answers Your customers already wrote your FAQ. Paste in reviews (yours or a competitor’s) and find out what people actually care about. The prompt Here are some customer reviews for a [type of business]. List the 5 things customers mention most (good or bad), then write a short FAQ answer for each that I could put on my website or say on the phone. Don’t invent facts about my business; leave a blank where you need my details. [paste reviews here] Copy prompt : Turn your reviews into answers Open in ChatGPT with the prompt for Turn your reviews into answers (opens in a new tab) For anyone Read the fine print in plain English A lease clause, a warranty, a bill you don’t understand. Get the plain version and the questions to ask before you sign or pay. The prompt Explain this in plain English, like you’re talking to a friend. Then list anything that could cost me money or lock me in, and 3 questions I should ask before I agree. I know this isn’t legal advice. [paste the text here] Not legal advice. For anything big, ask a lawyer, or see if you qualify for free help from the Legal Aid Society of Northeastern New York (lasnny.org). Copy prompt : Read the fine print in plain English Open in ChatGPT with the prompt for Read the fine print in plain English (opens in a new tab) For shop owners Make sure your hours match everywhere Wrong hours on Google is the fastest way to lose a walk-in. Do a two-minute check once a month. The prompt Make me a 5-minute monthly checklist to make sure my business hours, phone number and address are the same on Google, my website, Facebook, Yelp and Apple Maps. Include where to click on each one to fix it, and what to update before holidays. Copy prompt : Make sure your hours match everywhere Open in ChatGPT with the prompt for Make sure your hours match everywhere (opens in a new tab) Want it to just happen? Step 5 The shop confirms It's a request until the shop taps Confirm. Leave an email and you'll get the confirmation. No app, no hold music. Shops the line knows Barbers Salons Plumbers Heating & HVAC Electricians Mechanics Cleaners Locksmiths Emergency? Call 911. This line is not for emergencies. For a fire, a medical emergency, or someone in danger, call 911. If you smell gas, leave the building first, then call 911 or your gas utility's emergency line. If you describe an emergency on the line, it will tell you to call 911. If you're thinking about hurting yourself, call or text 988, the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, any time. If someone mentions self-harm on the line, it gives them 988 as well as 911. What the line never does — Pretend to be a person. — Say “booked” before the shop confirms. — Give a caller's details to a shop that hasn't signed up. — Handle emergencies. — Take payments. Not signed up? The line can still mention your shop with its Google rating and read out your public phone number, so the caller calls you directly. Signing up lets the line send you the job. Questions: hello@albanyaiguy.com FAQ Questions people ask Is the line live? + Not yet. 518-726-COOL is the planned number and it isn't connected, so please don't dial it yet. Email hello@albanyaiguy.com and you'll hear when it goes live. Am I talking to a real person? + No. The line is an AI assistant and says so at the start of every call. A real local shop gets your request and calls you back. Does it cost callers anything? + No. We don't charge callers. Your phone plan's normal calling rates apply. Is my appointment booked when I hang up? + Not yet. It's a request until the shop taps Confirm. If you leave an email, you'll get the confirmation, and the shop calls you to lock it in. Are calls recorded? + No. Call audio isn't recorded. Speech is turned into text in the moment so the line can understand you. If you make a request, only your first name, number, the time you want, and an optional email are saved and sent to the shop you chose. Can a business pay to be recommended first? + No. There is no paid ranking. The line recommends shops rated 4 stars or better on Google that have an opening. My shop isn't signed up. Can the line still mention it? + Yes. It can mention you with your Google rating and read out your public phone number so the caller calls you directly. Signing up lets the line send you the job instead. Where does it work? + Albany and the Capital Region: Schenectady, Troy, Saratoga Springs, and the towns around them. What about emergencies? + The line doesn't handle them. For a fire, a medical emergency, or a gas smell, leave if it's unsafe and call 911. For thoughts of self-harm, call or text 988, the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. More about the plan on the trunk line overview . Email me when it's live
